title: Phenol-based RNA extraction from polycarbonate filters
author: Robbie M. Martin
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bivuke6w
materials: Carefully decant ethanol supernatant without disturbing RNA pellet.

steps.title: Prepare Lysing Tube
steps.instruction: Prepare the bead beating tube with lysing buffer and chill.

substeps.instruction: Add 700 µL of Solution A (0.5% SDS, 20 mM sodium acetate, and 10 mM EDTA in RNase-free molecular biology grade water) to an MP Biomedical Lysing Matrix E tube (or equivalent).
Pre-chill the tube on ice to prevent overheating during bead beating.

steps.title: Add Polycarbonate Filter
steps.instruction: Introduce the sample filter into the prepared tube.

substeps.instruction: Unfold the polycarbonate filter (either frozen, or thawed but maintained on ice) and place it into the pre-chilled bead-beating tube.

steps.title: Initial Bead Beating
steps.instruction: Lyse the sample using high-speed agitation.

substeps.instruction: Agitate the tube on maximum speed for 40 s in a Biospec Products Mini-beadbeater (or equivalent).
Immediately place the tube on ice.

steps.title: First Phenol Extraction
steps.instruction: Perform initial extraction using basic phenol and chloroform.

substeps.instruction: Add 500 µL basic phenol with 8-hydroxyquinoline (pH 7.8-8.2) and 100 µL chloroform to the tube.
Agitate the tube on maximum speed for 40 s.
Place briefly on ice to chill.
Centrifuge at maximum speed in a benchtop centrifuge for 5 min.

steps.title: Recover Aqueous Phase
steps.instruction: Isolate the aqueous supernatant for further purification.

substeps.instruction: Transfer as much of the aqueous supernatant as possible from the bead beating tube to a new 2 mL centrifuge tube.

steps.title: Sequential Re-extractions
steps.instruction: Purify the RNA through a series of phenol and chloroform washes.

substeps.instruction: Re-extract the aqueous supernatant twice with 500 µL of acid phenol:chloroform:isoamyl alcohol (125:24:1; pH 4.8).
Re-extract the aqueous supernatant once with 500 µL basic phenol with 8-hydroxyquinoline plus 100 µL chloroform.
Re-extract twice with 500 µL pure chloroform to remove residual phenol.

steps.title: RNA Precipitation
steps.instruction: Precipitate the RNA from the aqueous phase.

substeps.instruction: Add sodium acetate to the aqueous supernatant to a final concentration of 0.3 M and mix.
Add 2-2.5x volume of ice-cold 100% ethanol and mix well.
Place in a -80 °C freezer for at least 1 h, or preferably overnight.

steps.title: Pellet the RNA
steps.instruction: Centrifuge to recover the RNA pellet.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge at maximum speed at 0 °C for at least 30 min in a refrigerated benchtop centrifuge (spin for 1 h if low yields are expected or to increase recovery).
Add 1 mL of ice-cold 70% ethanol and gently pipette to dislodge the RNA pellet.
Centrifuge at maximum speed at 0 °C for at least 15 min in a refrigerated benchtop centrifuge.
Gently and carefully aspirate as much of the 70% ethanol as possible without disturbing the pellet.

steps.title: Dry and Dissolve RNA
steps.instruction: Remove residual ethanol and resuspend the RNA.

substeps.instruction: Place the open tube in a 37 °C heating block for 3-5 min to evaporate ethanol (do not dry to completion).
Dissolve the RNA pellet in an appropriate amount of RNase-free water (typically 50-100 µL) based on expected yield and desired final concentration.
